data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

合同法：对价与赠与
⚖️ 核心法律原则 在美国合同法中，一个可执行的合同必须包含对价 (Consideration)。对价的核心要素是“经过讨价还价的交换” (Bargained-for Exchange)。

这意味着：
  • 一方的承诺必须“诱使”另一方做出承诺或行为。
  • 另一方的承诺或行为必须是前者承诺的“价格”。
🔍 案情深度剖析

本题的关键在于判断双方的电子邮件往来是否构成了“交换”。

  1. 男子的承诺：他说送书是因为“你一直是我的好朋友”。这是基于过去的行为 (Past Consideration) 或情感动机，属于赠与承诺 (Gift Promise)，而非为了换取任何东西。
  2. 朋友的回应：朋友说“谢谢，我打算送你蝴蝶收藏”。这虽然是一个回馈，但它并没有被男子所“索求”或“讨价还价”。

结论：这是两个独立的赠与承诺，而不是一个互为条件的合同。

✅ 正确答案解析
选项 D 支持男子，因为没有经过讨价还价的交换。

这是本题的题眼。男子的承诺是出于友情（Gift motive），而不是为了换取蝴蝶收藏。既然男子的承诺不是由朋友的承诺“诱发”的，就不存在 Bargained-for exchange。没有对价，承诺就不可强制执行。
❌ 干扰项陷阱
选项 A 关于“获益” (Benefit Conferred)
仅有获益不足以构成合同。虽然朋友交付蝴蝶让男子获益，但如果这个获益不是男子“讨价还价”得来的（即他没有要求用书换蝴蝶），它就不能作为支持送书承诺的对价。
选项 B 关于“信赖” (Reliance)
这涉及允诺禁反言 (Promissory Estoppel)。虽然朋友交付了蝴蝶，但通常要求这种信赖是“合理的”且是为了避免“实质性不公”。在MBE中，如果存在明显的“无对价”情况，且只是互赠礼物，法院很少会用禁反言原则来强制执行这种价值悬殊的赠与。
选项 C 关于“对价不充分” (Inadequacy)
这是一个经典的陷阱。法律通常不审查对价的充分性 (Adequacy of Consideration)。如果他们真的达成协议用$100换$10,000，只要是自愿交换，合同通常是有效的（Peppercorn Theory）。本案的问题不在于价值不对等，而在于根本没有“交换”。
💡 MBE 实战技巧
看到“因为你对我很好”、“作为感谢”等字眼时，警惕赠与 (Gift) 考点。

区分 Condition of a Gift（赠与的条件）与 Consideration（对价）：
  • "如果你来我家，我就送你大衣" → 来你家只是拿礼物的条件，不是对价。
  • "如果你帮我修剪草坪，我就送你大衣" → 修草坪是对价。
MBE Contracts Review | QID: Q81098

questions.question:
A real estate investor found a house for sale that he was interested in buying. The investor spoke with the owner of the house and sent her a written offer to purchase the house for $200,000. The offer stipulated that it would remain open for one month.
One week later, the investor suffered a stroke and was hospitalized. The stroke caused severe brain damage and permanent mental disability. The owner, having no knowledge of the investor's condition, decided to accept his offer. She signed the written offer and mailed it to the investor's address one day before the offer was set to expire. The investor received the signed offer two days later.
Is there an enforceable contract that binds the owner and the investor?

choices.a: No, because the investor received the acceptance after the stipulated one-month period.
choices.b: No, because the investor's offer terminated when he became permanently mentally incapacitated.
choices.c: Yes, because the owner had no knowledge of the investor's condition when she accepted his offer.
choices.d: Yes, because the owner mailed the acceptance within the stipulated one-month period.

data.questionStem:
Q81121

A real estate investor found a house for sale that he was interested in buying. The investor spoke with the owner of the house and sent her a written offer to purchase the house for $200,000. The offer stipulated that it would remain open for one month.

One week later, the investor suffered a stroke and was hospitalized. The stroke caused severe brain damage and permanent mental disability. The owner, having no knowledge of the investor's condition, decided to accept his offer. She signed the written offer and mailed it to the investor's address one day before the offer was set to expire. The investor received the signed offer two days later.

Is there an enforceable contract that binds the owner and the investor?

一名房地产投资者发现了一栋待售的房屋，并有兴趣购买。该投资者与房屋所有者进行了交谈，并向她发出了一份书面要约，愿意以20万美元的价格购买该房屋。该要约规定，其有效期为一个月。

一周后，该投资者中风并住院治疗。中风导致其严重的脑损伤和永久性精神残疾。房屋所有者在对投资者的情况不知情下，决定接受其要约。她在要约到期前一天签署了书面要约，并将其邮寄至投资者的地址。投资者在两天后收到了签署的要约。

在所有者和投资者之间，是否存在一份具有强制执行力的合同？
options:
A. No, because the investor received the acceptance after the stipulated one-month period.
否，因为投资者在规定的一月期限过后才收到承诺。

B. No, because the investor's offer terminated when he became permanently mentally incapacitated.
否，因为投资者的要约在其变为永久性精神丧失行为能力时即告终止。

C. Yes, because the owner had no knowledge of the investor's condition when she accepted his offer.
是，因为所有者在接受其要约时，对投资者的状况并不知情。

D. Yes, because the owner mailed the acceptance within the stipulated one-month period.
是，因为所有者在规定的一月期限内邮寄了承诺。
data.explanation:
An offer to form a contract generally remains open for the time stated in the offer or, if no time is stated, for a reasonable time. However, an offer will terminate prematurely if the offeror dies OR becomes permanently mentally incapacitated† before the offer is accepted - with one exception. An offer that is an option will not terminate under such circumstances because consideration was paid to keep the offer open for a specified period of time.

Here, the investor offered to buy the owner's house for $200,000. Although the offer stipulated that it would remain open for one month, it was not an option because the owner had not paid any consideration to keep the offer open. The investor then suffered a stroke that caused severe brain damage and permanent mental disability. The investor's permanent incapacity caused his offer to terminate prematurely, so the owner's subsequent attempt to accept it was ineffective. As a result, there is no contract that binds the parties.

†Permanent mental incapacity is presumed if there has been a formal adjudication that a party lacks the capacity to enter into a contract with another.

(Choices A & D) Under the mailbox rule, an acceptance that is mailed within the allotted response time is effective when it is sent - not when it is received. Because the owner's acceptance was mailed within the one-month period stipulated in the offer, it would have been effective had the investor's offer still been open.‡ But since the offer terminated when the investor became permanently mentally incapacitated, there is no contract.

‡ Had the offer specified that acceptance must be received within one month, the mailbox rule would not apply and the owner's acceptance would have been ineffective.

(Choice C) An offer terminates automatically upon death or permanent mental incapacity of the offeror (investor), regardless of the offeree's (owner's) knowledge thereof.

Educational objective: An offer will terminate if the offeror dies or becomes permanently mentally incapacitated prior to acceptance. However, an exception exists for an offer that is an option because consideration was paid to keep the offer open.



选项正确率统计：A选项 19%，B选项 33%（正确选项），C选项 13%，D选项 33%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

一份旨在订立合同的要约（offer），通常在要约中规定的时间内保持有效，若未规定时间，则在一段合理的时间内保持有效。然而，如果要约人在要约被承诺前死亡或变为永久性精神丧失行为能力†，要约将会提前终止——但有一个例外。在此等情况下，作为一项选择权的要约将不会终止，因为已有对价（consideration）支付以使该要约在特定时期内保持有效。

在本案中，投资者要约以20万美元购买所有者的房屋。尽管要约规定其有效期为一个月，但这并非一项选择权，因为所有者未支付任何对价以使该要约保持有效。随后，投资者中风，导致严重的脑损伤和永久性精神残疾。投资者的永久性丧失行为能力导致其要约提前终止，因此所有者随后的承诺行为是无效的。因此，双方之间不存在有约束力的合同。

†如果已有正式的司法裁定，认定一方当事人缺乏与他人订立合同的行为能力，则推定其为永久性精神丧失行为能力。

（选项 A & D）根据邮箱规则（mailbox rule），在指定答复时间内邮寄的承诺，于其发出时生效——而非收到时生效。因为所有者的承诺是在要约规定的一月期内邮寄的，所以如果投资者的要约仍然有效，该承诺本应是有效的。‡ 但由于要约在投资者变为永久性精神丧失行为能力时即告终止，因此不存在合同。

‡ 若要约明确规定承诺必须在一个月内被收到，则邮箱规则不适用，所有者的承诺将是无效的。

（选项 C）要约在要约人（投资者）死亡或永久性精神丧失行为能力时自动终止，无论受要约人（所有者）是否知晓此事。

教学目标： 如果要约人在承诺前死亡或永久性精神丧失行为能力，要约将终止。然而，作为一项选择权的要约是一个例外，因为已有对价支付以使该要约保持有效。

References

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 48 cmt. b (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (offer terminates when offeror is permanently deprived of capacity to contract).

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 12 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (capacity to contract).

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Termination of Offer

✓ 正确答案：B

本题考查的核心法律原则是：要约因法律实施而终止（Termination by Operation of Law），具体涉及要约人的死亡或丧失行为能力。

核心法则 (The Rule)

根据普通法（Common Law），如果要约人（Offeror）在要约被承诺（Acceptance）之前死亡或永久丧失行为能力（Permanently Incapacitated），要约将自动终止。

例外情况： 如果该要约是一个选择权合约（Option Contract）——即受要约人支付了对价（Consideration）以换取要约在特定时间内不可撤销——那么要约人的死亡或丧失行为能力不会终止要约。

案情分析 (Application)
1
要约的性质：投资者提出以20万美元买房，并称要约有效期为一个月。但这仅仅是一个“裸承诺”（naked promise），因为房主没有支付任何对价（Consideration）来购买这个时间窗口。因此，这不是Option Contract。
2
事件发生：投资者中风导致永久性精神残疾。根据法律，这属于丧失缔约能力。
3
法律后果：在投资者丧失行为能力的那一刻，要约自动终止。此时，房主尚未寄出承诺信。
4
结论：当房主后来寄出信件时，已经没有有效的要约可供承诺了。因此，合同不成立。
为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 C (关于知情权)：
这是最强的干扰项。许多考生认为只有受要约人“知道”对方出事了，要约才失效。
纠正：死亡或丧失行为能力导致的终止是自动的，不以受要约人知情为前提（这与“撤销要约 Revocation”不同，撤销通常需要通知到达才生效）。
选项 A & D (关于邮箱规则 Mailbox Rule)：
邮箱规则规定承诺在“投邮时生效”。但是，该规则适用的前提是要约在投邮那一刻仍然有效。
在本案中，要约在投邮前已经因为投资者丧失行为能力而“死亡”了。既然没有活着的要约，邮箱规则就无从谈起。
💡 MBE 考试技巧

在处理Offer Termination题目时，请按以下步骤思考：
1. 看是否有 Option Contract：如果有对价支付，要约人死了合同也能成立。
2. 看是 Common Law 还是 UCC：本题是房产（Common Law）。如果是货物买卖（UCC），要注意“Firm Offer”规则，但Firm Offer通常只限制要约人“撤销”的权利，并不一定能对抗死亡/丧失行为能力（除非转化为Option）。
3. 区分 Revocation 和 Operation of Law：
• 撤销（Revocation）通常需要受要约人收到通知。
• 死亡/丧失行为能力通常不需要通知即可终止要约。

Reference: Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 48

questions.question:
A wealthy rancher was drinking at a local bar. The rancher's neighbor walked into the bar, unaware of the rancher's intoxication. On several previous occasions, the neighbor had tried to persuade the rancher to sell his vintage muscle car, but the rancher had refused. Upon seeing the rancher, the neighbor said, "Hey, did you change your mind about selling me that vintage muscle car? I'll increase my offer to $15,000."
The rancher was annoyed and decided to play a joke on the neighbor. The rancher had no intention of selling his car but said, "Fine, I will sell you the car." The rancher then grabbed a napkin and wrote: "You finally bugged me enough! I will sell you my vintage muscle car for $15,000." The rancher signed the napkin and handed it to the neighbor. The neighbor happily walked away, believing that they had formed a binding agreement.
The following day, the neighbor approached the rancher to consummate the sale. The rancher refused to part with the car, claiming that he was intoxicated and merely joking when he wrote the note on the napkin.
If the neighbor sues the rancher for breach of contract, will the neighbor be likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because the rancher was joking when he wrote the note, so there was no meeting of the minds.
choices.b: No, because the rancher wrote the note while he was intoxicated, which renders the contract voidable.
choices.c: Yes, because the rancher's oral statement and written note were objective manifestations of his intent to enter a contract.
choices.d: Yes, because the written note estops the rancher from asserting any defense based on incapacity to contract.

一位富有的牧场主正在当地一家酒吧喝酒。牧场主的邻居走进酒吧，并不知道牧场主处于醉酒状态。在此前的几个场合，邻居曾试图说服牧场主出售他的老式肌肉车，但牧场主都拒绝了。看到牧场主后，邻居说：“嘿，关于卖给我那辆老式肌肉车的事，你改变主意了吗？我把我的要约提高到15,000美元。”

牧场主感到很烦，决定和邻居开个玩笑。牧场主无意出售他的车，但却说：“好吧，我把车卖给你。”牧场主随后抓起一张餐巾纸写道：“你总算把我烦够了！我将以15,000美元的价格把我的老式肌肉车卖给你。”牧场主在餐巾纸上签了名，并递给了邻居。邻居高兴地走开了，相信他们已经达成了具有约束力的协议。

第二天，邻居找到牧场主以完成这笔交易。牧场主拒绝交出汽车，声称他在餐巾纸上写字条时喝醉了，而且只是在开玩笑。

如果邻居以违约为由起诉牧场主，邻居是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because the rancher was joking when he wrote the note, so there was no meeting of the minds.
不会，因为牧场主写字条时是在开玩笑，所以双方没有达成意思表示一致。

B. No, because the rancher wrote the note while he was intoxicated, which renders the contract voidable.
不会，因为牧场主是在醉酒状态下写的字条，这使得合同可被撤销。

C. Yes, because the rancher's oral statement and written note were objective manifestations of his intent to enter a contract.
会，因为牧场主的口头声明和书面字条是他订立合同意图的客观表示。

D. Yes, because the written note estops the rancher from asserting any defense based on incapacity to contract.
会，因为该书面字条使牧场主不得主张任何基于无缔约能力的抗辩。
data.explanation:
Contract formation requires mutual assent (ie, offer and acceptance). During the negotiation process, the parties are entitled to rely on a reasonable interpretation of each other's words and actions since they cannot know each other's subjective intent. This means that a contract is formed when both parties objectively express their assent to enter a binding agreement. Once formed, the contract cannot be rescinded because of one party's secret intent not to be bound.

Here, the neighbor offered to buy the rancher's muscle car for $15,000. This was an objective expression of his intent to enter a contract, particularly since he had tried to buy the car on several previous occasions. The rancher orally accepted this offer and wrote the agreement on a napkin (objective assent), without giving any indication that he was joking (secret intent). Therefore, a contract was formed, and the neighbor is likely to prevail in his breach-of-contract suit.

(Choice A) At common law, contract formation required a subjective "meeting of the minds." The modern rule, however, looks to the parties' objective expressions of assent. Therefore, it is irrelevant that the rancher was subjectively joking and that there was no actual meeting of the minds.

(Choice B) A contract entered while intoxicated is voidable by the intoxicated party if:
  • that party was too intoxicated to reasonably understand the nature or consequences of the contract and
  • the other party had reason to know about the intoxication.
Here, there is no indication that the rancher was intoxicated to this extent. And since the neighbor had just walked into the bar, he had no reason to know that the rancher was intoxicated.

(Choice D) Both oral and written contracts are voidable by a party who lacked capacity at the time of formation. Therefore, the written note does not estop (ie, prevent) the rancher from asserting an incapacity defense.

Educational objective: Contract formation requires mutual assent, which occurs when both parties objectively convey their assent to enter a binding agreement. The resulting contract cannot be rescinded due to one party's secret intent not to be bound.

合同成立需要双方合意（即要约与承诺）。在谈判过程中，由于各方无法知晓对方的主观意图，他们有权依赖对彼此言行的合理解释。这意味着，当双方客观地表达了他们达成一项有约束力协议的同意时，合同即告成立。合同一旦成立，不能因一方当事人不愿受其约束的秘密意图而被撤销。

在本案中，邻居要约以15,000美元购买牧场主的肌肉车。这是他订立合同意图的客观表示，特别是因为他之前曾多次尝试购买该车。牧场主口头接受了此要约，并在餐巾纸上写下协议（客观同意），并未透露他是在开玩笑（秘密意图）。因此，合同已经成立，邻居很可能在违约之诉中胜诉。

（选项A）在普通法中，合同的成立需要主观上的“意思表示一致”。然而，现代规则着眼于当事人双方同意的客观表达。因此，牧场主主观上是在开玩笑以及双方实际上没有达成意思表示一致，这一点是无关紧要的。

（选项B）在醉酒状态下订立的合同，如果符合以下条件，醉酒方可以撤销：
  • 该方当事人醉酒程度严重，以至于无法合理理解合同的性质或后果，并且
  • 另一方当事人有理由知道其醉酒状态。
在本案中，没有迹象表明牧场主的醉酒程度达到了这种地步。而且由于邻居是刚走进酒吧，他没有理由知道牧场主喝醉了。

（选项D）无论是口头合同还是书面合同，在订立时缺乏行为能力的一方均可主张撤销。因此，该书面字条并不能禁止（即，阻止）牧场主提出无行为能力的抗辩。

教学目的：合同的成立需要双方合意，而双方合意在双方当事人客观地传达了他们愿意达成一项有约束力协议的意愿时即告发生。由此产生的合同不能因为一方当事人不愿受其约束的秘密意图而被撤销。

References

Lucy v. Zehmer, 196 Va. 493, 503 (1954) (finding a binding contract for the sale of a farm even though the seller was drinking and possibly joking when he signed the agreement).

MBE 考点解析

Contract Formation & Mutual Assent
✅ 正确答案：选项 C
核心考点：同意的客观理论

本题考查合同法中最基础也最重要的概念之一：同意的客观理论 (Objective Theory of Assent)。

在判断合同是否成立时，法律不看当事人内心真实的、秘密的想法（Subjective Intent），而是看当事人的言行举止在客观上是否向一个合理的旁观者传达了订立合同的意图。

经典判例：Lucy v. Zehmer (1954)
⚖️ 判例背景

这道题几乎完全复刻了美国合同法著名的 Lucy v. Zehmer 案。在该案中，两人在喝酒时，一人在餐厅账单背面写下了出售农场的协议。事后卖方声称自己只是在“开玩笑”且“喝醉了”。

法院判决：合同有效。因为卖方的行为（写下协议、签名、讨论细节）客观上表现出了缔约意图，买方有理由相信这是真实的交易。

本题深度解析
📝
客观表现 (Objective Manifestation)：
牧场主不仅口头同意，还拿餐巾纸写下了具体的条款（价格 $15,000，标的物 Muscle Car），并签了名。对于邻居（合理的旁观者）来说，这完全符合一份正式合同的特征。
🤫
秘密意图 (Secret Intent)：
牧场主内心想“开玩笑”是主观的。只要他没有把“我在开玩笑”表现出来，他的内心戏在法律上是无关紧要的。
🍺
醉酒抗辩 (Intoxication Defense)：
这是本题的干扰项。醉酒确实可能使合同可撤销 (Voidable)，但必须满足两个条件：
  • 一方醉到无法理解交易性质；且
  • 另一方有理由知道 (Reason to know) 对方醉了。
题目明确指出邻居“不知道 (unaware)”牧场主醉酒，因此该抗辩不成立。
为什么其他选项是错的？
  • 选项 A (错)： 提到“没有达成意思表示一致 (Meeting of the minds)”。这是旧普通法的概念。现代合同法不要求主观上的“心意相通”，只要求客观上的行为一致。
  • 选项 B (错)： 仅凭“醉酒”不能自动让合同无效或可撤销。关键在于对方是否知情（Good faith purchaser protection）。
  • 选项 D (错)： 书面形式并不能阻止（Estop）当事人提出无行为能力（Incapacity）的抗辩。如果邻居知道牧场主烂醉如泥，即使写在纸上，合同依然可能被撤销。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
看到“开玩笑 (Joke)”或“虚张声势 (Bluff)”的题目，立即联想客观理论。如果玩笑开得太逼真，让对方当真了，合同通常是成立的！

questions.question:
A businesswoman entered into a contract with a painter by the terms of which he was to paint the businesswoman's office for $1,000 and was required to do all the work over the following weekend so as to avoid disruption of her business.
If the painter had started to paint on the following Saturday morning, he could have finished before Sunday evening. However, he stayed home that Saturday morning and did not start to paint until Saturday afternoon. By late Saturday afternoon, the painter realized that he had underestimated the time it would take to finish the job if he continued to work alone. The painter phoned the businesswoman at her home and accurately informed her that it was impossible to finish the work over the weekend unless he hired a helper. He also stated that to do so would require an additional charge of $200 for the work. The businesswoman told the painter that she apparently had no choice but to pay "whatever it takes" to get the work done as scheduled.
The painter hired an assistant to help finish the painting and paid him $200. The businesswoman has offered to pay the painter $1,000. The painter is demanding $1,200.
How much is the painter likely to recover?

choices.a: $1,000 only, because the businesswoman received no consideration for her promise to pay the additional sum.
choices.b: $1,000 only, because the businesswoman's promise to pay "whatever it takes" is too uncertain to be enforceable.
choices.c: $1,200, because the impossibility of the painter's completing the work alone discharged the original contract and a new contract was formed
choices.d: $1,200, in order to prevent the businesswoman's unjust enrichment.

一位女商人与一名油漆工签订合同，合同条款规定油漆工为其办公室粉刷，报酬为1000美元，并要求在接下来的周末完成所有工作，以避免影响其业务。

如果油漆工在周六早上开始粉刷，他本可以在周日晚上之前完工。然而，他周六早上待在家里，直到周六下午才开始动工。到了周六下午晚些时候，油漆工意识到，如果他继续独自工作，他低估了完成工作所需的时间。油漆工打电话给女商人的家里，准确地告知她，除非他雇一个帮手，否则不可能在周末完成工作。他还表示，这样做需要额外支付200美元的费用。女商人告诉油漆工，她显然别无选择，只能支付“任何必要的代价”来按时完成工作。

油漆工雇了一名助手来帮助完成粉刷工作，并支付了200美元。女商人提出支付油漆工1000美元。油漆工要求1200美元。

油漆工很可能收回多少钱？
options:
A. $1,000 only, because the businesswoman received no consideration for her promise to pay the additional sum.
仅1000美元，因为女商人为支付额外款项的承诺没有获得对价。

B. $1,000 only, because the businesswoman's promise to pay "whatever it takes" is too uncertain to be enforceable.
仅1000美元，因为女商人支付“任何必要的代价”的承诺过于不确定，无法强制执行。

C. $1,200, because the impossibility of the painter's completing the work alone discharged the original contract and a new contract was formed
1200美元，因为油漆工无法独自完成工作导致原合同解除，并成立了一份新合同。

D. $1,200, in order to prevent the businesswoman's unjust enrichment.
1200美元，以防止女商人的不当得利。
data.explanation:
Modifying existing contracts


Governing lawRequirements
Common lawTraditional view
Parties' agreement
New consideration

Modern view
Parties' agreement
New consideration unless modification is fair & equitable due to unanticipated circumstances
UCCParties' agreement
Good faith (ie, honesty & observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing)
New consideration not required
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

At common law, contract modifications must be supported by new consideration - ie, each party must alter its duties in some way - unless the modification is fair and equitable in light of unanticipated circumstances. But the promise to perform, or the performance of, a preexisting duty is insufficient for new consideration and cannot support a modification.

Here, the painter attempted to modify the $1,000 contract by telling the businesswoman that he needed to hire a helper, which would require an additional charge of $200. Although the businesswoman agreed to pay "whatever it takes," the painter had a preexisting duty to finish painting over the weekend. Therefore, the businesswoman received no consideration for her promise to pay the additional sum, and the painter is likely to recover $1,000 only.

(Choice B) There is no consideration if either party makes an illusory promise - ie, one that essentially pledges nothing because it is too uncertain (or because the promising party can choose whether to honor it). But the businesswoman's promise to pay "whatever it takes" was not too uncertain since it was a response to the painter's statement that he needed an additional $200 to finish the work.

(Choice C) Contractual duties can be discharged due to impossibility - eg, when an unanticipated or extraordinary event makes it impossible to perform. But here, the painter's inability to finish the work was due to his own delay - not an unanticipated or extraordinary event.

(Choice D) A party may recover restitution damages to prevent unjust enrichment if the party conferred a non-gratuitous benefit on another without a contractual obligation to do so. Here, the painter conferred a non-gratuitous benefit by paying the helper $200 to finish the work. However, since the painter was already obligated to paint the office for $1,000, the businesswoman was not unjustly enriched by his expenditure.

Educational objective: At common law, contract modifications generally must be supported by new consideration, which requires both parties to alter their duties in some way. Performing or promising to perform a preexisting duty is insufficient for consideration and will not support a modification.

选项正确率统计：A选项 89%（正确选项），B选项 3%，C选项 3%，D选项 2%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

修改现有合同


管辖法律要求
普通法 (Common law)传统观点
双方协议
新的对价

现代观点
双方协议
新的对价 除非 因未预见的情况而修改是公平合理的
UCC双方协议
善意（即诚实并遵守合理的商业公平交易标准）
不要求新的对价
UCC = 《统一商法典》(Uniform Commercial Code)

在普通法下，合同修改必须有新的对价支持——即，每一方都必须以某种方式改变其义务——除非鉴于未曾预料到的情况，该修改是公平合理的。但是，承诺履行或履行一项已存在的义务，对于新的对价而言是不充分的，并且不能支持合同修改。

在本案中，油漆工试图修改这份1000美元的合同，他告知女商人需要雇佣一名帮手，而这将需要额外支付200美元。尽管女商人同意支付“任何必要的代价”，但油漆工有在周末完成粉刷工作的已存义务。因此，女商人为支付额外款项的承诺没有获得对价，油漆工很可能只能收回1000美元。

（选项B）如果任何一方作出了虚幻的承诺——即，因其过于不确定（或因为承诺方可以选择是否履行）而实质上未承诺任何事情的承诺，则不存在对价。但是，女商人支付“任何必要的代价”的承诺并非过于不确定，因为这是对油漆工声称需要额外200美元来完成工作的回应。

（选项C）合同义务可因履行不能而解除——例如，当一个未预见或异常的事件使得履行成为不可能时。但在本案中，油漆工无法完成工作是由于他自己的延误——而非未预见或异常的事件。

（选项D）如果一方在没有合同义务的情况下向另一方提供了非无偿的利益，该方可以获得返还性损害赔偿，以防止不当得利。在本案中，油漆工通过支付帮手200美元来完成工作，提供了非无偿的利益。然而，由于油漆工已有义务以1000美元的价格粉刷办公室，女商人并未因他的支出而构成不当得利。

教学目标：在普通法下，合同修改通常必须有新的对价支持，这要求双方都以某种方式改变其义务。履行或承诺履行一项已存义务不足以构成对价，也不能支持合同修改。

References

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 73 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that performance of a preexisting legal duty is not consideration).

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 89 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that modification of a contract without new consideration is binding if it is fair and equitable in view of unanticipated circumstances).

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Preexisting Duty Rule
⚖️ 核心法律规则：既有义务规则 (Preexisting Duty Rule)

在普通法 (Common Law) 下，修改合同必须有新的对价 (New Consideration) 支持。如果一方只是承诺履行其原本就已经有法律义务去履行的职责，这不能构成新的对价。

✅ 正确答案分析 (选项 A)
结论：油漆工只能收回 $1,000。

推理逻辑：
  1. 适用法律：本案涉及服务合同（粉刷办公室），因此适用普通法 (Common Law)，而非《统一商法典》(UCC)。
  2. 既有义务：根据原合同，油漆工有义务在周日晚前完成工作，报酬为 $1,000。
  3. 缺乏对价：油漆工要求额外 $200 只是为了完成他原本就承诺要做的事情（按时完工）。虽然他雇佣了助手，但这只是他履行原合同义务的方式，并没有给女商人提供任何新的法律利益 (Legal Benefit)，女商人也没有获得额外的服务。
  4. 结果：女商人承诺支付额外费用的协议因缺乏对价 (Lack of Consideration) 而无效。
❌ 干扰项排除
选项 B (不确定性)：错误。
虽然“whatever it takes”听起来模糊，但在本案语境下，它是对油漆工明确提出的 $200 额外费用的回应，因此金额是确定的。该承诺无效的原因是缺乏对价，而不是条款不确定。
选项 C (履行不能/新合同)：错误。
只有当发生不可预见且客观上无法履行的事件 (Objective Impossibility) 时，合同才会被解除。本案中，无法完工是因为油漆工自己“周六早上待在家里”导致的延误，属于主观不能，且是自找的麻烦，不能作为解除合同的理由。
选项 D (不当得利)：错误。
不当得利 (Unjust Enrichment) 适用于没有合同依据但一方获益的情况。这里双方有明确的 $1,000 合同。女商人支付了 $1,000 获得了约定的粉刷服务，这是公平交易，不存在“不当”得利。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
遇到“合同修改”题目时，第一步先判断是服务 (Common Law) 还是货物 (UCC)。
  • 如果是 Common Law：修改必须有对价 (Consideration)。
  • 如果是 UCC：修改只需善意 (Good Faith)，不需要对价。
本题是典型的 Common Law 陷阱题。

questions.question:
Upon entering a bank to open an account, a customer read a poster on the bank's wall that said, "New Customers! $25 FOR 5 MINUTES. If you stand in line for more than five minutes, we will pay you $25! We like happy customers!" The customer stood in line and started timing his wait. Just as five minutes was about to pass, the bank manager tore the poster down and announced, "The $25 stand-in-line promotion is over." The customer waited in line for 10 more minutes before being served.
Does the customer have a claim against the bank for $25?

choices.a: No, because the bank withdrew its offer before the customer completed the requested performance.
choices.b: No, because the bank's statement was a nonbinding gift promise.
choices.c: Yes, because the bank could not revoke its offer once the customer had commenced performance.
choices.d: Yes, because the customer's presence in line served as notice to the bank that he had accepted.

data.questionStem:
Q81065

Upon entering a bank to open an account, a customer read a poster on the bank's wall that said, "New Customers! $25 FOR 5 MINUTES. If you stand in line for more than five minutes, we will pay you $25! We like happy customers!" The customer stood in line and started timing his wait. Just as five minutes was about to pass, the bank manager tore the poster down and announced, "The $25 stand-in-line promotion is over." The customer waited in line for 10 more minutes before being served.

Does the customer have a claim against the bank for $25?

一位顾客进入银行开户时，看到墙上有一张海报写着：“新顾客！5分钟25美元。如果您排队超过五分钟，我们将支付您25美元！我们希望顾客满意！”该顾客开始排队并计时。就在五分钟即将结束时，银行经理撕下海报并宣布：“25美元排队促销活动结束。”该顾客又在队伍中等待了10分钟才获得服务。

该顾客是否有权向银行索赔25美元？
options:
A. No, because the bank withdrew its offer before the customer completed the requested performance.
无权，因为银行在该顾客完成所要求的履行之前撤回了其要约。

B. No, because the bank's statement was a nonbinding gift promise.
无权，因为银行的声明是一个不具约束力的赠与承诺。

C. Yes, because the bank could not revoke its offer once the customer had commenced performance.
有权，因为一旦顾客已经开始履行，银行就不能撤销其要约。

D. Yes, because the customer's presence in line served as notice to the bank that he had accepted.
有权，因为顾客排队的行为构成了他已接受要约的通知。
data.explanation:
Bilateral v. Unilateral contracts


OfferEffect of beginning performance
UnilateralInvites acceptance by performance of actCreates option contract that prevents offeror from revoking offer
Offeree is not bound to complete performance
BilateralInvites acceptance by return promiseServes as acceptance of offer
Offeree is bound to complete performance
An offer to form a unilateral contract arises when one party (ie, offeror) invites another party (ie, offeree) to accept an offer only by performing a specified act. The offer becomes irrevocable once the offeree begins performance, thereby creating an option contract - ie, a separate agreement under which the offer will remain open and irrevocable for a period of time. The offer is accepted once the offeree completes the requested performance, and a binding unilateral contract is formed.†

Here, the bank's poster offered to pay $25 to any new customer who stood in line for more than five minutes. The new customer read the poster and began performance by standing in line, so the manager could not subsequently withdraw the offer by tearing the poster down and announcing that the promotion was over (Choice A). A binding contract was then formed when the customer completed performance by waiting in line for the specified time. As a result, the customer has a claim against the bank for breaching that contract by failing to pay him $25.

†If the offeree begins but fails to complete the requested performance (ie, partial performance), there is no contract because only complete performance constitutes an acceptance of the offer. As a result, the offeror cannot assert a breach-of-contract claim against the offeree in that scenario.

(Choice B) The bank's statement was not a gift promise because the $25 was offered in exchange for a legal detriment - ie, standing in line for more than five minutes when the customer had no legal obligation to do so.

(Choice D) The customer's presence in line merely created an option contract since a unilateral contract can only be accepted by completing the requested performance. But had the bank offered to form a bilateral contract, the customer's presence in line (ie, beginning of performance) would have served as notice of his acceptance.

Educational objective: To form a unilateral contract, an offeror must invite the offeree to accept an offer by performing a specified act. An irrevocable option contract is created once the offeree begins performance. A binding unilateral contract will then be formed if the offeree accepts the offer by fully performing the specified act.

选项正确率统计：A选项 14%，B选项 5%，C选项 73%（正确选项），D选项 6%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

双边合同与单边合同


要约开始履行的效果
单边合同以履行行为的方式邀请承诺产生一个选择权合同，使要约人无法撤销要约
受要约人没有义务完成履行
双边合同以对待承诺的方式邀请承诺构成对要约的承诺
受要约人有义务完成履行
当一方（即要约人）邀请另一方（即受要约人）仅通过履行特定行为来接受要约时，便产生了旨在形成单边合同的要约。一旦受要约人开始履行，该要约即变为不可撤销，从而产生一个选择权合同——即一个独立的协议，据此要约将在一段时间内保持开放且不可撤销。一旦受要约人完成所要求的履行，该要约即被承诺，一个具有约束力的单边合同就此成立。†

在本案中，银行的海报要约向任何排队超过五分钟的新顾客支付25美元。该新顾客看到了海报，并通过排队开始履行，因此经理不能通过撕下海报并宣布促销结束的方式来撤回要约（选项A）。当该顾客通过排队达到规定时间从而完成履行时，一个具有约束力的合同便已成立。因此，该顾客有权因银行未能向其支付25美元而违反该合同，向银行提出索赔。

†如果受要约人开始但未能完成所要求的履行（即部分履行），则不存在合同，因为只有完全履行才构成对要约的承诺。因此，在这种情况下，要约人不能对受要约人提出违约索赔。

（选项B）银行的声明不是赠与承诺，因为25美元是为换取一种法律上的损害（legal detriment）而提供的——即在顾客没有法律义务的情况下排队超过五分钟。

（选项D）顾客排队的行为仅仅产生了一个选择权合同，因为单边合同只能通过完成所要求的履行来承诺。但是，如果银行的要约是旨在形成一个双边合同，那么顾客排队的行为（即开始履行）将构成其承诺的通知。

教学目标：为形成单边合同，要约人必须邀请受要约人通过履行特定行为来接受要约。一旦受要约人开始履行，即产生一个不可撤销的选择权合同。如果受要约人通过完全履行特定行为来接受要约，那么一个具有约束力的单边合同就将成立。

References

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 45 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that an option contract is formed when an offeree begins performance after an offer to form a unilateral contract).

data.htmlContent:
单边合同与要约撤销

MBE Contracts Key Concept
核心考点：单边合同 (Unilateral Contract)

本题考查的是单边合同中，要约人何时失去撤销要约的权利（Power of Revocation）。

关键区别：

  • 双边合同 (Bilateral)： 以承诺换取承诺（Promise for Promise）。
  • 单边合同 (Unilateral)： 以承诺换取行为（Promise for Performance）。只有完成行为才算承诺。
法律规则：Restatement (Second) § 45

在单边合同要约中，一旦受要约人开始履行 (Begins Performance)：

  1. 即产生一个选择权合同 (Option Contract)。
  2. 要约人暂时失去撤销权，必须给受要约人合理的时间去完成履行。
  3. 受要约人虽然开始了，但没有义务必须完成（除非双方另有约定）。
  4. 只有当受要约人完全履行 (Completes Performance) 时，合同才正式成立并需支付对价。

本案分析

1
要约性质：银行海报写着“排队超过5分钟给25美元”。这是典型的单边合同要约，因为它寻求的是顾客的行为（排队），而非口头承诺。
2
开始履行：顾客开始排队并计时。此时，顾客已经开始履行 (Commenced Performance) 要约所要求的行为。
3
撤销无效：根据规则，一旦开始履行，要约就变得不可撤销 (Irrevocable)。银行经理撕海报的行为发生在顾客开始排队之后，因此撤销无效。
4
最终结果：顾客完成了要求的行为（排队总共15分钟 > 5分钟）。合同成立，银行必须支付25美元。

为什么选 C？

选项 C 正确。 它准确陈述了现代合同法（Restatement）的规则：一旦开始履行，要约人就不能撤销要约。

其他选项为何错误？

选项 错误原因
A 这是旧普通法（Old Common Law）的规则（即“布鲁克林大桥案”旧例），认为只有完全履行前一秒都能撤销。现代法律已废除此规则，以防止不公。
B 不是赠与（Gift）。顾客付出了“法律上的损害”（Legal Detriment），即花时间排队，构成了有效的约因（Consideration）。
D 单边合同通常不需要“通知”（Notice）来承诺，而是通过“履行”来承诺。排队本身是履行行为，产生不可撤销性，而非仅仅作为通知。
🎓 MBE 考试技巧：

遇到“悬赏广告”或“完成某事给钱”的题目：
1. 确认是单边合同（Promise for Act）。
2. 检查受要约人是否已经开始履行（不仅仅是准备履行）。
3. 如果已经开始，要约人不能撤销。
4. 记住关键词：Option Contract (选择权合同) 是保护受要约人的机制。

questions.question:
A debtor owed a lender $1,500. The statute of limitations barred recovery on the claim. The debtor wrote to the lender, stating, "I promise to pay you $500 if you will extinguish the debt." The lender agreed.
Is the debtor's promise to pay the lender $500 enforceable?

choices.a: No, because the debtor made no promise not to plead the statute of limitations as a defense.
choices.b: No, because there was no consideration for the debtor's promise.
choices.c: Yes, because the debtor's promise provided a benefit to the lender.
choices.d: Yes, because the debtor's promise to pay part of the barred antecedent debt needs no consideration to be enforceable.

data.questionStem:
Q81101

A debtor owed a lender $1,500. The statute of limitations barred recovery on the claim. The debtor wrote to the lender, stating, "I promise to pay you $500 if you will extinguish the debt." The lender agreed.

Is the debtor's promise to pay the lender $500 enforceable?

一名债务人欠一名债权人1500美元。诉讼时效已过，该债权无法追偿。债务人致信债权人，称：“若您免除此债务，我承诺向您支付500美元。”债权人同意了。

债务人支付500美元的承诺是否具有强制执行力？
options:
A. No, because the debtor made no promise not to plead the statute of limitations as a defense.
否，因为债务人并未承诺不以诉讼时效为抗辩理由。

B. No, because there was no consideration for the debtor's promise.
否，因为债务人的承诺缺乏对价。

C. Yes, because the debtor's promise provided a benefit to the lender.
是，因为债务人的承诺为债权人提供了利益。

D. Yes, because the debtor's promise to pay part of the barred antecedent debt needs no consideration to be enforceable.
是，因为债务人支付部分已过时效的先前债务的承诺，无需对价即可强制执行。
data.explanation:
Exceptions to preexisting duty rule


Main rulePromise to perform (or performance of) preexisting duty is not consideration
New/altered considerationNew duty added or preexisting duty altered (eg, acceleration of due date)
Ratification of voidable dutyNew promise to perform voidable duty (eg, upon reaching age of majority)
Common law exceptionsHonest dispute Scope of duty honestly disputed Unexpected event Fair & equitable modification in view of unanticipated circumstances Renewed promise Renewed promise to pay preexisting debt despite technical defense (eg, statute of limitations, bankruptcy) if written or partially performed Third party Preexisting duty owed to third party (ie, nonparty to contract at issue)
UCC exceptionModification Modification sought in good faith - ie, honesty and observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

A promise to perform a preexisting duty is generally unenforceable for lack of consideration. But under a long-established exception to this rule, a debtor's renewed promise to pay all or part of a preexisting debt is enforceable if:
  • the debtor renewed the promise despite the existence of a technical defense to recovery of the original debt (eg, statute of limitations, bankruptcy) and
  • the renewed promise was made in writing or partially performed.
Here, the statute of limitations barred recovery on the lender's claim against the debtor for $1,500. Despite this defense, the debtor made a renewed promise to pay $500 of the preexisting debt. And though there was no consideration for this promise, it was made in a written letter (Choice B). Therefore, the debtor's promise to pay $500 is enforceable without consideration.

(Choice A) Although the debtor made no promise to waive his statute-of-limitations defense, his renewed promise to pay part of the debt is still enforceable since it was made in writing despite being time-barred. And that promise will defeat the statute-of-limitations defense with respect to $500 of the debt.

(Choice C) Early case law described the consideration requirement in terms of benefit to the promisee (here, the lender), whereas modern courts focus instead on legal detriment to the promisor (here, the debtor). But whether the debtor's promise was a benefit or a detriment is irrelevant because consideration is not required.

Educational objective: A promise to perform a preexisting duty is generally unenforceable. But a debtor's renewed promise to pay all or part of a preexisting debt is enforceable if the debtor renewed his/her promise despite a technical defense (eg, statute of limitations) AND the renewed promise was made in writing or partially performed.

选项正确率统计：A选项 1%，B选项 24%，C选项 18%，D选项 55%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

先前存在义务规则的例外


主要规则履行（或已履行）先前存在义务的承诺不构成对价
新的/变更的对价增加新义务或变更先前存在义务（例如，提前到期日）
对可撤销义务的追认履行可撤销义务的新承诺（例如，达到法定成年年龄时）
普通法例外善意争议 义务范围存在善意争议 意外事件 鉴于未预见情况而进行的公平合理的变更 更新的承诺 尽管存在技术性抗辩（例如，诉讼时效、破产），但对先前存在债务作出的支付承诺，如以书面形式或已部分履行，则为更新的承诺 第三方 对第三方（即非本案合同当事人）负有的先前存在义务
UCC例外变更 善意寻求的变更——即，诚实并遵守合理的商业公平交易标准
UCC = 《统一商法典》(Uniform Commercial Code)

履行先前存在义务的承诺通常因缺乏对价而无强制执行力。但根据该规则一项早已确立的例外，债务人更新的支付全部或部分先前存在债务的承诺具有强制执行力，前提是：
  • 债务人作出更新承诺时，明知对原债务的追偿存在技术性抗辩（例如，诉讼时效、破产）并且
  • 该更新的承诺是书面的或已部分履行的。
在本案中，诉讼时效已过，债权人对债务人的1500美元债权无法追偿。尽管存在此抗辩，债务人仍作出了支付500美元先前存在债务的更新承诺。并且，虽然该承诺没有对价，但它是以书面信函形式作出的（选项B）。因此，债务人支付500美元的承诺无需对价也具有强制执行力。

（选项A）尽管债务人并未承诺放弃其诉讼时效抗辩，但他支付部分债务的更新承诺仍然具有强制执行力，因为该承诺是在债务已过时效的情况下以书面形式作出的。并且，该承诺将使针对这500美元债务的诉讼时效抗辩无效。

（选项C）早期的判例法从受诺人（此处指债权人）获得的利益角度来描述对价的要求，而现代法院则更关注出诺人（此处指债务人）遭受的法律上的损害。但债务人的承诺是利益还是损害在此无关紧要，因为本案无需对价。

教学目标：履行先前存在义务的承诺通常不具有强制执行力。但是，如果债务人在明知存在技术性抗辩（如诉讼时效）的情况下仍更新其支付全部或部分先前存在债务的承诺，并且该更新的承诺是以书面形式作出或已部分履行，那么该承诺就具有强制执行力。

References

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that a renewed promise to pay a preexisting debt is binding if that debt would be binding except for the statute of limitations).

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Consideration & Moral Obligation
🔑 核心法律规则 (The Rule)

一般原则是：履行先前存在的义务（Pre-existing Duty）不构成有效的对价（Consideration）。

但是，存在一个重要例外：

如果一项债务因诉讼时效 (Statute of Limitations) 而无法强制执行，债务人作出的新的书面承诺（或部分履行）可以使该债务（或承诺的部分）重新具有强制执行力，且无需新的对价。

案情分析 (Case Analysis)

本案中，关键事实如下：

  1. 原债务：$1,500，但已被诉讼时效（SOL）阻断，法律上无法强制追偿。
  2. 新行为：债务人写信（Written Promise）承诺支付 $500。
  3. 法律后果：虽然原债务在法律上已“死”，但债务人的书面新承诺使其“复活”了。

根据《合同法重述（第二版）》§ 82，这种承诺具有约束力，且仅需以新承诺的范围为限（即 $500）。

选项深度解析
正确答案 D

理由：这直接陈述了普通法中的例外规则。对于已过诉讼时效的先前债务（Barred Antecedent Debt），债务人支付部分的承诺无需对价即可强制执行。

这里的关键在于“无需对价”这一特殊性，它是基于道德义务（Moral Obligation）演变而来的法律拟制。

选项 B 错误

理由：选项 B 错误地应用了“一般规则”。虽然通常承诺需要对价，但本题考查的正是不需要对价的例外情况。如果考生只记得“没有对价就没有合同”，就会误选此项。

选项 A 错误

理由：法律不要求债务人明确说出“我放弃诉讼时效抗辩”这样的话。只要债务人作出了新的书面支付承诺，法律效果上就等同于放弃了针对这 $500 的时效抗辩。

选项 C 错误

理由：虽然这看起来像是一个“利益交换”，但现代合同法分析并不依赖于债权人是否获得了“利益”。本案强制执行的依据是法定例外，而非传统的利益/受损（Benefit/Detriment）对价分析。

💡 MBE 备考锦囊：

在 Contracts 题目中，当你看到“债务” (Debt) + “诉讼时效已过” (Statute of Limitations has run) + “新承诺” (New Promise) 的组合时：

  • 立即寻找“书面” (Written) 或 “部分履行” (Partially Performed) 的细节。
  • 如果满足上述条件，该承诺无需对价即可执行。
  • 注意：执行范围仅限于新承诺的金额（本案是 $500，而非原债 $1,500）。

questions.question:
A developer owned 250 lots in a new residential development. A builder of single-family homes approached the developer with a signed, written offer "to purchase a block of lots for a reasonable price to be determined by the market." Prior to that, three other residential construction companies had each purchased blocks of 50 lots from the developer for between $75,000 and $90,000 per lot, depending on lot size and location. The developer signed the builder's offer upon receiving it. A week later, the developer notified the builder that the developer had sold the remaining 100 lots to another builder.
If the builder sues the developer for breach of contract, will the builder be likely to prevail?

choices.a: No, because all essential terms must be specified in the contract for the contract to be valid.
choices.b: No, because the contract is voidable by the developer since the actual market price was not stated in the agreement.
choices.c: Yes, because the court can use the other construction companies' purchases to "fill the gap" for the missing quantity and price terms.
choices.d: Yes, because the parol evidence rule does not bar extrinsic evidence of the reasonable market price.

一名开发商在一个新的住宅开发项目中拥有250块地块。一名独栋住宅的建筑商向该开发商提交了一份经签署的书面要约，表示“愿以市场决定的合理价格购买一批地块”。在此之前，另外三家住宅建筑公司各自以每块75,000至90,000美元不等的价格（取决于地块大小和位置）从该开发商处购买了50块地块。开发商在收到建筑商的要约后便签署了该要约。一周后，开发商通知该建筑商，其已将剩余的100块地块出售给了另一位建筑商。

如果该建筑商以违约为由起诉开发商，建筑商是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because all essential terms must be specified in the contract for the contract to be valid.
不会，因为合同若要有效，所有基本条款都必须在合同中明确规定。

B. No, because the contract is voidable by the developer since the actual market price was not stated in the agreement.
不会，因为实际市场价格未在协议中说明，因此开发商可以撤销该合同。

C. Yes, because the court can use the other construction companies' purchases to "fill the gap" for the missing quantity and price terms.
会，因为法院可以利用其他建筑公司的购买记录来“填补”缺失的数量和价格条款。

D. Yes, because the parol evidence rule does not bar extrinsic evidence of the reasonable market price.
会，因为口头证据规则不排除关于合理市场价格的外部证据。
data.explanation:
Essential contract terms


PartiesSubject matter (eg, description of goods or services)
Price or other considerationQuantity
Duration of contractTime for each party's performance
†Necessarily varies by contract

At common law, all essential terms must be covered in a contract for it to be valid and enforceable. Those terms must be sufficiently certain and definite for the court to determine the existence of a breach and give an appropriate remedy. Otherwise, the contract fails for indefiniteness.†

One essential term is the subject matter of the agreement - eg, a description of the property to be sold in a land-sales contract. A property description is sufficiently certain and definite if it enables the court to determine exactly what property is being sold. Here, the description ("block of lots") is too indefinite to make such a determination. As a result, the builder is unlikely to prevail.

†Indefiniteness may be cured by surrounding circumstances or conduct by the parties that permits the court to supply the term. But here, there are no such circumstances or acts by the parties to identify exactly which lots were to be sold.

(Choice B) Although the actual market price was not stated in the agreement, "reasonable market price" is a sufficiently certain and definite price term since market value can be determined objectively. Also, had this essential term been missing or otherwise insufficient, the contract would have been void - not voidable.

(Choice C) The Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) encourages contract formation by "filling the gap" for many missing terms - including price but not quantity. Additionally, land-sales contracts are governed by common law - not the UCC, which governs contracts for the sale of goods.

(Choice D) The parol evidence rule generally bars extrinsic evidence of prior or contemporaneous agreements to modify or contradict the terms of a final written agreement. However, evidence of the reasonable market price is not barred by this rule.

Educational objective:

At common law, all essential terms must be covered in an agreement, and those terms must be sufficiently certain and definite. The property description in a land-sales contract meets this standard if it allows the court to determine the exact property being sold.

选项正确率统计：A选项 74%（正确选项），B选项 4%，C选项 17%，D选项 3%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

合同基本条款


当事人标的物（例如，货物或服务的描述）
价格或其他对价数量
合同期限各方履行时间
†因合同而异

在普通法下，一份合同若要有效且可强制执行，其必须涵盖所有基本条款。这些条款必须足够确定和明确，以便法院能够判断是否存在违约行为并给出适当的救济。否则，合同会因不确定性而无效。†

其中一个基本条款是协议的标的物——例如，在土地销售合同中对待售财产的描述。如果财产描述能让法院准确判断出正在出售的是哪块财产，那么该描述就是足够确定和明确的。在本案中，“一批地块”的描述过于不明确，无法做出这样的判断。因此，建筑商不太可能胜诉。

†不确定性可以通过周围情况或当事人的行为来补救，从而允许法院补充该条款。但在本案中，没有任何此类情况或当事人行为可以确定究竟要出售哪些地块。

(选项 B) 尽管协议中未说明实际市场价格，但“合理的市场价格”是一个足够确定和明确的价格条款，因为市场价值可以被客观地确定。此外，如果这个基本条款缺失或不充分，合同将是无效的——而不是可撤销的。

(选项 C) Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) 鼓励通过“填补”许多缺失的条款来促成合同的成立——包括价格，但不包括数量。此外，土地销售合同受普通法管辖——而不受管辖货物销售合同的 UCC 管辖。

(选项 D) 口头证据规则通常禁止使用先前或同期的协议的外部证据来修改或反驳最终书面协议的条款。然而，关于合理市场价格的证据并不受此规则的禁止。

教学目标：

在普通法下，协议必须涵盖所有基本条款，并且这些条款必须足够确定和明确。土地销售合同中的财产描述若能让法院确定正在出售的确切财产，则符合此标准。

References

17A Am. Jur. 2d Contracts § 180 (2020) (requisites for definiteness and certainty of contract terms).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

合同法：不确定性与基本条款

✅ 正确答案分析

本题的正确答案是 A。

核心理由：在普通法（Common Law）管辖下，合同必须包含所有基本条款 (Essential Terms)，且这些条款必须足够明确。

本案涉及不动产销售 (Sale of Land)，适用普通法而非 UCC。对于土地合同，必须明确指明：

  • 当事人 (Parties)
  • 价格 (Price)
  • 标的物描述 (Description of Property)

题目中“a block of lots”（一批地块）的描述过于模糊。法院无法确定究竟是哪几块地、多少块地。由于标的物无法确定，合同因不确定性 (Indefiniteness)而无法执行。

⚖️ 法律规则详解

1. 适用法律：普通法 vs. UCC

这是解题的第一步。涉及土地权益的合同适用Common Law。如果是货物买卖（如木材、钢筋），则适用UCC Article 2。

2. 确定性要求 (Certainty and Definiteness)

规则：普通法要求合同条款必须足够明确，以便法院能够确定是否存在违约并给予救济（如特定履行 Specific Performance）。

在本案中，虽然价格条款（"reasonable price"）可能通过市场价值确定，但数量和具体位置完全缺失。对于房地产而言，每一块土地都被视为是独一无二的（Unique），因此必须准确描述。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？

选项 C (Gap Filling)：

这是最强的干扰项。考生容易混淆 UCC 和普通法。

  • UCC： 允许法院“填补空白” (Gap Fillers)，只要双方有缔约意图，即使缺少价格条款合同也可能成立。但即便是 UCC，通常也要求数量 (Quantity) 必须明确。
  • 普通法： 很少允许法院填补基本条款的空白，尤其是土地销售中的标的物描述。法院不会替当事人重写合同。

选项 B (Void vs. Voidable)：

如果缺少基本条款，合同在法律上是自始无效 (Void)，即合同从未成立；而不是可撤销 (Voidable)。此外，价格条款并非本案的致命伤，标的物不明才是。

选项 D (Parol Evidence Rule)：

虽然口头证据规则 (PER) 确实允许引入解释性证据，但 PER 的前提是存在一个有效的书面合同。本案的问题在于合同本身因缺乏确定性而未成立，因此 PER 并非主要争点。

💡 MBE 备考锦囊

  1. 识别标的物： 看到“Land”、“Real Estate”、“Lots” -> 立即反应适用 Common Law。
  2. 检查基本条款： 普通法对合同成立的要求比 UCC 严格得多。检查是否缺少：Parties, Price, Property description, Quantity (PPPQ)。
  3. 警惕“填补空白”： 如果是普通法题目，选项中出现“法院可以填补缺失条款”通常是错误的（除非是细枝末节的非基本条款）。

questions.question:
A bakery offered a chef a permanent full-time job as a pastry chef at a salary of $3,000 per month. The chef agreed to take the position and to begin work in two weeks. In her employment application, the chef had indicated that she was seeking a permanent job.
One week after the chef was hired by the bakery, a hotel offered the chef a position as a restaurant manager at a salary of $3,500 a month. The chef accepted and promptly notified the bakery that she would not report for work at the bakery.
Is the bakery likely to prevail in a lawsuit against the chef for breach of contract?

choices.a: No, because a contract for permanent employment would be interpreted to mean that the chef could leave at any time.
choices.b: No, because the position the chef took with the hotel was not substantially comparable to the one she had agreed to take with the bakery.
choices.c: Yes, because the chef's acceptance of a permanent position meant that she agreed to leave the bakery only after a reasonable time.
choices.d: Yes, because the chef's failure to give the bakery a chance to match the salary offered by the hotel breached the implied right of first refusal.

Q81074

A bakery offered a chef a permanent full-time job as a pastry chef at a salary of $3,000 per month. The chef agreed to take the position and to begin work in two weeks. In her employment application, the chef had indicated that she was seeking a permanent job.

One week after the chef was hired by the bakery, a hotel offered the chef a position as a restaurant manager at a salary of $3,500 a month. The chef accepted and promptly notified the bakery that she would not report for work at the bakery.

Is the bakery likely to prevail in a lawsuit against the chef for breach of contract?

一家烘焙店向一位厨师提供了一份月薪3000美元的永久性全职糕点师工作。该厨师同意接受该职位，并于两周后开始工作。在她的工作申请中，该厨师已表明她正在寻求一份永久性工作。

在该厨师被烘焙店雇用一周后，一家酒店向她提供了一个月薪3500美元的餐厅经理职位。该厨师接受了该职位，并立即通知烘焙店她将不会去报到上班。

在对该厨师提起的违约诉讼中，烘焙店是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because a contract for permanent employment would be interpreted to mean that the chef could leave at any time.
不会，因为一份永久雇佣合同将被解释为厨师可以随时离职。

B. No, because the position the chef took with the hotel was not substantially comparable to the one she had agreed to take with the bakery.
不会，因为厨师在酒店接受的职位与她同意在烘焙店接受的职位不具有实质上的可比性。

C. Yes, because the chef's acceptance of a permanent position meant that she agreed to leave the bakery only after a reasonable time.
会，因为厨师接受永久性职位意味着她同意只在一段合理的时间后才能离开烘焙店。

D. Yes, because the chef's failure to give the bakery a chance to match the salary offered by the hotel breached the implied right of first refusal.
会，因为厨师未能给予烘焙店机会以提供与酒店相当的薪水，这违反了默示的优先承购权。
data.explanation:
Employment contracts


Definite durationTermination allowed only for cause or by mutual agreement
Indefinite durationPermanent durationAt-will employment can be terminated by either party at any time & for any reason

Exception: termination violates public policy
A contract to employ someone for an indefinite or permanent duration typically creates an at-will employment relationship. An at-will employment relationship allows either party to terminate the employment contract at any time and for any reason unless the termination violates public policy - eg, when an employee is discharged for filing a discrimination claim.

Here, the contract for permanent employment formed an at-will employment relationship that allowed the chef to leave the bakery at any time (Choice C). The chef's termination of the employment contract did not violate public policy because society wants at-will employees to be free to take on new opportunities. Therefore, the chef did not breach the contract by accepting the job with the hotel, and the bakery is unlikely to prevail.

(Choice B) Whether the position the chef took with the hotel is substantially comparable to the position at the bakery would be relevant had the bakery breached the contract. In this scenario, the chef would have then had a duty to mitigate damages by making reasonable efforts to secure comparable employment.

(Choice D) A right of first refusal is an express contractual right that gives the holder of the right the option to contract with a party before anyone else. This right cannot be created by implication.

Educational objective: A contract for permanent employment creates an at-will employment relationship that entitles either party to terminate the contract at any time and for any reason, without the termination being considered a breach.

选项正确率统计：A选项 69%（正确选项），B选项 4%，C选项 21%，D选项 4%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

雇佣合同


固定期限仅可因正当理由或双方协议终止
不定期限永久期限自由雇佣关系可由任何一方在任何时间以任何理由终止

例外：终止行为违反公共政策
雇佣某人期限为不定期或永久的合同，通常会建立一种自由雇佣关系。自由雇佣关系允许任何一方在任何时间以任何理由终止雇佣合同，除非该终止行为违反公共政策——例如，当雇员因提起歧视申诉而被解雇时。

在本案中，这份永久性雇佣合同构成了一种自由雇佣关系，允许厨师随时离开烘焙店（选项C）。厨师终止雇佣合同的行为并未违反公共政策，因为社会希望自由雇佣的雇员能够自由地寻求新的机会。因此，厨师接受酒店的工作并未构成违约，烘焙店也不太可能胜诉。

（选项B）厨师在酒店接受的职位是否与在烘焙店的职位具有实质可比性，这一点只有在烘焙店违约的情况下才具有相关性。在那种情况下，厨师将有减损义务，即通过做出合理努力来获得可比的雇佣机会。

（选项D）优先承购权是一种明示的合同权利，它赋予权利持有人在任何其他人之前与一方订立合同的选择权。该权利不能通过默示方式创设。

教学目标：一份永久雇佣合同会建立一种自由雇佣关系，该关系赋予任何一方在任何时间以任何理由终止合同的权利，且该终止不被视为违约。

References

27 Am. Jur. 2d Employment Relationship § 30 (2020) (explaining that a permanent employment agreement is an at-will employment contract).

MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Employment Agreements

本题的正确答案是 A。

核心考点在于美国合同法中对“永久性雇佣”（Permanent Employment）的默认解释规则。

⚖️ 核心法律规则 在美国普通法中，除非合同明确规定了具体的雇佣期限（如“为期一年”），否则雇佣关系被推定为自由雇佣(At-will Employment)。

这意味着：
  • 雇主可以随时解雇员工（只要不违反公共政策或反歧视法）。
  • 员工可以随时辞职。
  • 不需要提供理由，也不需要承担违约责任。
案情深度解析

题目中明确指出，烘焙店提供的是一份“永久性全职工作”(permanent full-time job)，且厨师申请的也是“永久性工作”。

在法律解释上，“永久性”并不意味着“终身”，而是指“无限期”(Indefinite duration)。既然期限是不确定的，它就落入了自由雇佣的范畴。

因此，厨师有权在任何时候终止合同，包括在正式入职之前。既然她有权终止，她的行为就不构成违约(Breach of Contract)。

选项辨析
✅ 选项 A (正确)
正确指出了法律后果。永久雇佣合同被解释为允许任何一方随时终止关系。因此，烘焙店不会胜诉。
❌ 选项 B (错误)
“实质上的可比性”(Substantially comparable) 是计算损害赔偿时的减损义务(Mitigation of damages) 概念。只有当确定一方违约后，才讨论这个问题。本题中厨师并未违约，因此该选项无关。
❌ 选项 C (错误)
自由雇佣关系不需要给予“合理时间”(Reasonable time)。权利是即时的。
❌ 选项 D (错误)
优先承购权/优先拒绝权(Right of first refusal) 必须是合同中明示的条款，不能通过默示产生。
💡MBE 考试技巧：
看到 "Permanent Employment"（永久雇佣）这个词时，大脑要立刻反应出 "At-will"（自由雇佣）。

除非题目中出现了具体的时间段（如 "for 2 years"）或者限制解雇的条款（如 "only for cause"），否则默认任何一方都可以随时拍屁股走人而不承担法律责任。

questions.question:
A home goods retailer, in a signed writing, contracted with an apartment complex for the sale to the apartment complex of 50 identical sets of specified bathroom faucets, 25 sets to be delivered on March 1, and the remaining 25 sets on April 1. The agreement did not specify the place of delivery, or the time or place of payment.
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.a: The home goods retailer has no duty to deliver the 25 sets on March 1 at the retailer's place of business unless the apartment complex tenders the contract price for the 25 sets on that date.
choices.b: The home goods retailer must deliver 25 sets on March 1, and the apartment complex must pay the contract price for the 25 sets within a reasonable time after their delivery.
choices.c: The home goods retailer must deliver 25 sets on March 1, but the apartment complex's payment is due only upon the delivery of all 50 sets.
choices.d: The home goods retailer must tender 25 sets to the apartment complex at the complex's place of business on March 1, but does not have to turn them over to the complex until it pays the contract price for the 25 sets.

data.questionStem:
Q81089

A home goods retailer, in a signed writing, contracted with an apartment complex for the sale to the apartment complex of 50 identical sets of specified bathroom faucets, 25 sets to be delivered on March 1, and the remaining 25 sets on April 1. The agreement did not specify the place of delivery, or the time or place of payment.

Which of the following statements is correct?

一家家居用品零售商通过一份经签署的书面文件，与一栋公寓大楼签订合同，向该公寓大楼出售50套指定的同款浴室水龙头，其中25套于3月1日交付，其余25套于4月1日交付。该协议未明确交货地点，也未明确付款时间或地点。

下列哪项陈述是正确的？
options:
A. The home goods retailer has no duty to deliver the 25 sets on March 1 at the retailer's place of business unless the apartment complex tenders the contract price for the 25 sets on that date.
除非公寓大楼在3月1日当日为该25套水龙头支付合同价款，否则该家居用品零售商无义务在其营业地交付这25套水龙头。

B. The home goods retailer must deliver 25 sets on March 1, and the apartment complex must pay the contract price for the 25 sets within a reasonable time after their delivery.
该家居用品零售商必须在3月1日交付25套水龙头，而公寓大楼必须在交付后的合理时间内为这25套水龙头支付合同价款。

C. The home goods retailer must deliver 25 sets on March 1, but the apartment complex's payment is due only upon the delivery of all 50 sets.
该家居用品零售商必须在3月1日交付25套水龙头，但公寓大楼的付款义务仅在全部50套水龙头交付后才到期。

D. The home goods retailer must tender 25 sets to the apartment complex at the complex's place of business on March 1, but does not have to turn them over to the complex until it pays the contract price for the 25 sets.
该家居用品零售商必须于3月1日，在公寓大楼的营业地提示交付25套水龙头，但在公寓大楼为这25套水龙头支付合同价款之前，不必将货物移交给对方。
data.explanation:
UCC gap fillers


(effect of missing terms) Missing termsGap fillers
Place of delivery
  • Seller's place of business if applicable
  • Seller's home
  • Some other place if parties know goods are there
Time for shipment/deliveryReasonable time
PriceReasonable price at time for delivery
Time/place for paymentTime & place buyer is to receive goods
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

Contracts for the sale of goods (eg, faucets) are governed by Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). The UCC "fills the gap" when certain terms are missing from a contract. For example, the gap filler for a missing place of delivery is generally the seller's place of business if the seller has one. And unless the contract specifies otherwise, payment is due at the time and place the buyer is to receive each shipment of goods. In that case, the seller is only required to deliver the goods if the buyer tenders the payment.

Here, the home goods retailer contracted to sell bathroom faucets to the apartment complex. The time for delivery is specified (ie, 25 sets on March 1 and 25 sets on April 1). But since the place of delivery is missing, it must be made at the retailer's place of business - not the apartment complex's (Choice D). And since the time and place for payment are also missing, the contract price for the first 25 sets is due on March 1 (Choices B & C). Therefore, the retailer has no duty to deliver these sets unless the apartment complex tenders payment on that date.

Educational objective: The UCC fills the gap when certain terms are missing from a sale-of-goods contract. For example, the gap filler for the place of delivery is generally the seller's place of business if the seller has one. And unless the contract specifies otherwise, payment is due at the time and place the buyer is to receive each shipment of goods.

选项正确率统计：A选项 9%（正确选项），B选项 54%，C选项 25%，D选项 10%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

UCC 缺省条款填补规则


（缺失条款的效力）缺失条款缺省填补规则
交货地点
  • 如适用，则为卖方的营业地
  • 卖方的住所
  • 如双方知晓货物所在地，则为该其他地点
装运/交货时间合理时间
价格交货时的合理价格
付款时间/地点买方接收货物的时间和地点
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code (美国统一商法典)

货物（例如水龙头）的销售合同受《Uniform Commercial Code》(UCC) 第二条管辖。当合同中某些条款缺失时，UCC 会“填补空白”。例如，对于缺失的交货地点，缺省填补规则通常是卖方的营业地（如果卖方有营业地）。而且，除非合同另有规定，付款义务在买方接收每批货物的时间和地点到期。在这种情况下，只有在买方支付货款时，卖方才有义务交付货物。

在本案中，家居用品零售商签约向公寓大楼出售浴室水龙头。交货时间已明确（即3月1日交付25套，4月1日交付25套）。但由于交货地点缺失，交货必须在零售商的营业地进行，而不是公寓大楼的营业地（选项D）。并且，由于付款时间和地点也缺失，首批25套水龙头的合同价款应于3月1日支付（选项B和C）。因此，除非公寓大楼在该日支付货款，否则零售商无义务交付这批货物。

教学目标：当货物销售合同中某些条款缺失时，UCC会填补空白。例如，对于交货地点的缺省填补规则通常是卖方的营业地（如果卖方有营业地）。而且，除非合同另有规定，付款义务在买方接收每批货物的时间和地点到期。

References

  • U.C.C. § 2-308 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (providing gap filler when place for delivery is missing).
  • U.C.C. § 2-310 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (providing gap filler when time and place for payment are missing).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

UCC 缺省条款 (Gap Fillers)

Contracts / Sales (UCC Art. 2)
📝 案情摘要：
零售商与公寓签订书面合同，销售50套水龙头。约定分两批交付（3月1日和4月1日各25套）。
关键点：合同未约定交货地点、付款时间或地点。
1. 法律适用 (Applicable Law) 本案涉及货物买卖（水龙头），因此适用《统一商法典》第二篇 (UCC Article 2)。
核心考点：UCC 缺省规则

当合同对某些条款保持沉默时，UCC 会自动填补这些空白（Gap Fillers）。

📍 交货地点 (Place of Delivery):
根据 UCC § 2-308，除非另有约定，交货地点为卖方的营业地 (Seller's place of business)。

⏰ 付款时间 (Time of Payment):
根据 UCC § 2-310，除非另有约定，付款应在买方收到货物的时间和地点 (Time and place of receipt)进行。

2. 逻辑推演 (Legal Reasoning)
  • 由于合同未规定地点，零售商不需要把货送到公寓（排除选项 D）。零售商只需在自己的店里把货准备好供买方提取。
  • 由于合同未规定付款时间，且这是分批交付 (Installment Contract)，买方有义务在收到每一批货物时支付该批货物的价款（排除选项 C）。
  • 并发条件 (Concurrent Conditions): 在非信用交易中，交货和付款是并发条件。卖方不给钱不交货，买方不交货不给钱。
3. 为什么选项 A 是正确的？

选项 A 准确结合了上述两个规则：

  1. 地点正确：提到“在零售商的营业地 (at the retailer's place of business)”。
  2. 条件正确：零售商没有义务交货，除非 (unless) 公寓大楼提示付款 (tenders payment)。这体现了“一手交钱，一手交货”的原则。
🚫 陷阱辨析
  • 选项 B 错误：付款不是在交货后“合理时间内”，而是在“收到货物时”立即到期。
  • 选项 C 错误：在分批交货合同中，如果价格可以分割，卖方可以要求对每一批次单独付款 (UCC § 2-307)，而不是等全部交完才付。
  • 选项 D 错误：UCC 默认交货地是卖方处，而非买方处。
✅ 正确答案：A
MBE 备考策略：遇到合同条款缺失，优先回忆 UCC Gap Fillers。

questions.question:
An elderly woman asked her neighbor perform maintenance on the woman's property in exchange for apples from the woman's apple trees. The neighbor was happy to enter into this agreement, as the trees produced high-quality apples that he could subsequently sell at markets. He told the woman that the offer sounded very appealing and that he would discuss it with his wife. The neighbor also told the woman that he would stop by her home the next day to give her a final answer. The woman immediately called her children to tell them that she likely had someone to take over maintenance responsibilities. The next day, the neighbor learned that the woman had died in her sleep. Two days later, the woman's children approached the neighbor and asked when he would begin work.
Which of the following accurately describes how the neighbor may proceed?

choices.a: The neighbor may accept a new offer in accordance with terms proposed by the woman's children.
choices.b: The neighbor may accept the offer in accordance with the original terms.
choices.c: The neighbor may enforce the terms of the contract he entered with the woman.
choices.d: The neighbor may use the defense of impracticability to avoid being held to the terms of the original offer.

questions.question:
On November 1, an accountant and a lawyer contracted for the sale of the law books the accountant had inherited from his father. The lawyer agreed to pay the purchase price of $10,000 when the accountant delivered the books on December 1.
On November 10, the lawyer received a signed letter from the accountant that stated: "I have decided to dispose of the bookshelves containing the law books you have already purchased. If you want the shelves, I will deliver them to you along with the books on December 1 at no additional cost to you. Let me know before November 15 whether you want them. I will not sell them to anyone else before then." On November 14, the lawyer faxed and the accountant received the following message: "I accept your offer of the shelves." The accountant was not a merchant with respect to either law books or bookshelves.
Why is the accountant contractually obligated to deliver the shelves?

choices.a: Because the accountant's letter (received by the lawyer on November 10) and the lawyer's fax message of November 14 constituted an effective modification of the original sale-of-books contract.
choices.b: Because the accountant's letter (received by the lawyer on November 10) waived the bargained-for consideration that would otherwise be required.
choices.c: Because the lawyer provided a new bargained-for exchange by agreeing to take the shelves.
choices.d: Because the lawyer's fax message of November 14 operated to rescind unilaterally the original sale-of-books contract.

data.questionStem:
Q81135

On November 1, an accountant and a lawyer contracted for the sale of the law books the accountant had inherited from his father. The lawyer agreed to pay the purchase price of $10,000 when the accountant delivered the books on December 1.

On November 10, the lawyer received a signed letter from the accountant that stated: "I have decided to dispose of the bookshelves containing the law books you have already purchased. If you want the shelves, I will deliver them to you along with the books on December 1 at no additional cost to you. Let me know before November 15 whether you want them. I will not sell them to anyone else before then." On November 14, the lawyer faxed and the accountant received the following message: "I accept your offer of the shelves." The accountant was not a merchant with respect to either law books or bookshelves.

Why is the accountant contractually obligated to deliver the shelves?

11月1日，一名会计师和一名律师签订了一份买卖该会计师从其父亲那里继承的法律书籍的合同。律师同意在会计师于12月1日交付书籍时，支付10,000美元的购买价款。

11月10日，律师收到会计师签署的一封信，信中写道：“我已决定处理掉存放您已购买的法律书籍的书架。如果您想要这些书架，我将在12月1日将它们与书籍一同交付给您，您无需支付额外费用。请在11月15日之前告知我您是否想要。在此之前我不会将它们卖给任何其他人。” 11月14日，律师传真了以下信息，且会计师已收到：“我接受您关于书架的要约。”就法律书籍或书架而言，该会计师并非商人。

为什么该会计师有合同义务交付书架？
options:
A. Because the accountant's letter (received by the lawyer on November 10) and the lawyer's fax message of November 14 constituted an effective modification of the original sale-of-books contract.
因为会计师的信件（律师于11月10日收到）和律师于11月14日发出的传真信息，构成了对原始书籍买卖合同的有效变更。

B. Because the accountant's letter (received by the lawyer on November 10) waived the bargained-for consideration that would otherwise be required.
因为会计师的信件（律师于11月10日收到）放弃了本应被要求的、经协商的对价。

C. Because the lawyer provided a new bargained-for exchange by agreeing to take the shelves.
因为律师通过同意接收书架，提供了一个新的经协商的交换。

D. Because the lawyer's fax message of November 14 operated to rescind unilaterally the original sale-of-books contract.
因为律师于11月14日发出的传真信息单方面地解除了原始的书籍买卖合同。
data.explanation:
Modifying existing contracts


Governing lawRequirements
Common law
  • Traditional view
    Parties' agreement New consideration
  • Modern view
    Parties' agreement New consideration unless modification is fair & equitable due to unanticipated circumstances
UCC
  • Parties' agreement Good faith (ie, honesty & observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing)
  • New consideration not required
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

Contracts for the sale of goods (eg, law books) are governed by Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). Under the UCC , an existing contract cannot be modified or rescinded unilaterally (Choice D). Instead, all parties must agree to the modification. Additionally, the modification must be sought in good faith , which requires honesty and observance of reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing. But new consideration - ie, a bargained-for exchange of promises or performance that was not part of the original contract - is not required.

Here, the lawyer contracted to buy law books from the accountant for $10,000. Both parties agreed to modify that contract when the lawyer (1) received the accountant's letter offering to deliver the bookshelves with the books and (2) accepted that offer by fax. There is no indication that either party acted in bad faith. And since new consideration was not required to modify the contract, the accountant is contractually obligated to deliver the books and the shelves (Choice B).

(Choice C) The lawyer's agreement to take the shelves did not provide a new bargained-for exchange because the accountant was going to dispose of the shelves anyway. In other words, the accountant was not induced by the lawyer's agreement. But this is immaterial since consideration is not required to modify a sale-of-goods contract.

Educational objective: Under the UCC, a contract for the sale of goods can be modified by agreement of all the parties if that modification is sought in good faith. New consideration is not required.

选项正确率统计：A选项 65%（正确选项），B选项 15%，C选项 18%，D选项 0%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

变更现有合同


管辖法律要求
普通法
  • 传统观点
    双方协议 新的对价
  • 现代观点
    双方协议 新的对价 除非 因未预见之情形导致变更属公平合理
UCC
  • 双方协议 善意（即，诚实及遵守合理的商业公平交易标准）
  • 不要求新的对价
UCC = 《统一商法典》(Uniform Commercial Code)

货物买卖合同（例如，法律书籍）受《统一商法典》(UCC) 第2条管辖。根据UCC，现有合同不能被单方面变更或解除（选项D）。反之，所有当事方必须同意此项变更。此外，变更必须本着善意提出，这要求诚实及遵守合理的商业公平交易标准。但是，不要求新的对价——即，不属于原始合同一部分的、经协商的允诺或履行之交换。

在本案中，律师与会计师签订合同，以10,000美元购买法律书籍。当律师 (1) 收到会计师提出将书架随书籍一同交付的信件，并 (2) 通过传真接受该要约时，双方同意变更该合同。没有迹象表明任何一方存在恶意。由于变更此合同无需新的对价，因此会计师有合同义务交付书籍和书架（选项B）。

（选项C） 律师同意接收书架并未提供新的经协商的交换，因为会计师本就打算处理掉这些书架。换言之，会计师并未受到律师同意的引诱。但这一点无关紧要，因为变更货物买卖合同无需对价。

教学目标：根据UCC，只要变更是本着善意提出的，货物买卖合同可以经所有当事方协议进行变更。变更无需新的对价。

References

U.C.C. § 2-209 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (modification of existing contracts).

MBE 考点解析：合同变更

本题的核心考点在于区分普通法 (Common Law) 与 《统一商法典》 (UCC) 对于合同变更要求的不同。

正确答案：A
因为根据 UCC，只要双方达成合意且出于善意，合同变更无需新的对价。

1. 法律适用分析 (Governing Law)

1 判断标的物：
本案涉及的是法律书籍 (Law Books) 和书架 (Bookshelves)。这些都是可移动的物品，属于货物 (Goods)。
2 确定法律：
货物买卖受 UCC Article 2 管辖，而非普通法。

2. 核心规则对比

这是 MBE 考试中经典的“陷阱”考点，请务必牢记以下区别：

规则体系 合同变更 (Modification) 的要求
普通法
Common Law		 需要新的对价 (New Consideration)。
遵循“既有义务规则” (Pre-existing Duty Rule)。
UCC
Article 2		 不需要对价 (No Consideration Needed)。
只需要双方善意 (Good Faith) 地达成协议。

3. 案情具体分析

  • 原始合同：律师以 $10,000 购买书籍。
  • 提议变更：会计师提议免费赠送书架（即增加卖方的义务，而不增加买方的付款）。
  • 接受：律师通过传真接受了该提议。

推理逻辑：

如果这是服务合同（普通法），会计师的承诺将不可执行，因为律师没有提供额外的钱（对价）来换取书架。但是，因为这是货物买卖 (UCC)，会计师赠送书架的承诺构成了对原合同的有效变更 (Effective Modification)。只要会计师是出于善意（想清理旧物），且双方同意，该变更即具有法律约束力。

4. 为什么其他选项是错误的？

  • 选项 B (Waiver of Consideration)： 虽然结果相似，但法律推理不准确。UCC 2-209(1) 直接废除了变更需要对价的要求，而不是说对价被“放弃”了。放弃 (Waiver) 通常用于一方放弃对方的某项履约条件，而本案是双方达成了一项新的变更协议。
  • 选项 C (New Bargained-for Exchange)： 错误。律师同意接收书架并不是一种“法律上的受损”或新的对价，因为会计师本就想处理掉它们。更重要的是，在 UCC 下根本不需要寻找新的对价。
  • 选项 D (Rescind)： 错误。单方面解除合同 (Unilateral Rescission) 是违约行为，除非合同有特殊规定。本案是双方协商一致的变更。
🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)：
在 MBE 合同法题目中，一旦看到“合同变更” (Modification) 的场景：
  1. 立即检查是服务/房产（普通法）还是货物（UCC）。
  2. 如果是货物，直接寻找“不需要对价，只要善意”的选项。
  3. 不要被“是否是商人” (Merchant) 迷惑。UCC 的变更规则适用于所有货物买卖，不仅限于商人（尽管商人的善意标准更高）。
Reference: UCC § 2-209 (Modification, Rescission and Waiver)

questions.question:
A homeowner and a contractor entered into a contract under which the homeowner agreed to pay the contractor $50,000 for remodeling the homeowner's basement according to a set of plans.
After the work was completed, the homeowner honestly believed that there were defects in the contractor's work as well as departures from the plans. In fact, the contractor had fully performed. The homeowner offered to pay the contractor $35,000 in full settlement in exchange for the contractor's promise to surrender his entire claim. The contractor accepted the homeowner's offer, and the homeowner paid the contractor $35,000. The reasonable value of the work was $35,000.
Is the contractor likely to succeed in an action challenging the validity of the settlement agreement?

choices.a: No, because the homeowner honestly disputed the amount he owed the contractor.
choices.b: No, because the reasonable value of the work was only $35,000.
choices.c: Yes, because the contractor reasonably relied on the homeowner's contractual promise to pay the full $50,000, and that promise should be enforced to avoid injustice.
choices.d: Yes, because the homeowner's payment of $35,000 cannot furnish consideration for the contractor's relinquishment of a claim for $50,000.

data.questionStem:
Q81829 A homeowner and a contractor entered into a contract under which the homeowner agreed to pay the contractor $50,000 for remodeling the homeowner's basement according to a set of plans.

After the work was completed, the homeowner honestly believed that there were defects in the contractor's work as well as departures from the plans. In fact, the contractor had fully performed. The homeowner offered to pay the contractor $35,000 in full settlement in exchange for the contractor's promise to surrender his entire claim. The contractor accepted the homeowner's offer, and the homeowner paid the contractor $35,000. The reasonable value of the work was $35,000.

Is the contractor likely to succeed in an action challenging the validity of the settlement agreement? 一位房主与一位承包商签订了一份合同，根据该合同，房主同意支付承包商$50,000，用于根据一套图纸改造房主的地下室。 工程完工后，房主善意地相信承包商的工程存在瑕疵并且偏离了图纸。事实上，承包商已经完全履行了合同。房主提议支付$35,000作为完全和解，以换取承包商承诺放弃其全部索赔。承包商接受了房主的提议，房主向承包商支付了$35,000。该工程的合理价值为$35,000。 承包商在质疑该和解协议有效性的诉讼中是否可能胜诉？
options:
A. No, because the homeowner honestly disputed the amount he owed the contractor.
不会，因为房主善意地对欠承包商的金额提出了争议。

B. No, because the reasonable value of the work was only $35,000.
不会，因为该工程的合理价值仅为$35,000。

C. Yes, because the contractor reasonably relied on the homeowner's contractual promise to pay the full $50,000, and that promise should be enforced to avoid injustice.
会，因为承包商合理地信赖了房主支付全部$50,000的合同承诺，为避免不公，该承诺应被强制执行。

D. Yes, because the homeowner's payment of $35,000 cannot furnish consideration for the contractor's relinquishment of a claim for $50,000.
会，因为房主支付的$35,000不能构成承包商放弃$50,000索赔的对价。
data.explanation:
Ways to discharge contractual obligations


Full performance of contractual obligations
Impossibility, impracticability, or frustration of purpose
Release (in writing only)
Mutual rescission
Substituted contract
Contract or covenant not to sue
Accord & satisfaction
Novation
Mnemonic: FIRM SCAN
One method of discharging contractual obligations is by an accord (new contract) and satisfaction (performance of the accord). An accord is created when the parties to a contract agree to give and accept something different in satisfaction of their existing contractual obligations. Since an accord is a new contract, it must be supported by consideration. Where the new consideration is worth less than what was agreed to in the original contract, it will only be sufficient if:
  • there is a good-faith dispute as to the amount owed or
  • the new consideration is of a different type than what was owed under the original contract (eg, goods in lieu of cash).


Here, the homeowner offered to pay the contractor $35,000 in full satisfaction of his contractual obligation to pay the contractor $50,000. The contractor agreed to that lesser amount (accord), and the homeowner paid it (satisfaction). Since the homeowner honestly believed that there were defects in the contractor's work and departures from the plans (good-faith dispute), the homeowner's payment of $35,000 furnished sufficient consideration to form a valid accord (Choice D). Therefore, the contractor will likely not succeed.

(Choice B) The fact that the reasonable value of the work was only $35,000 does not excuse the homeowner from his obligation to pay the $50,000 contract price. Instead, the homeowner's obligation was discharged by an accord (new contract for $35,000) and satisfaction (payment of the $35,000).

(Choice C) The doctrine of promissory estoppel enables a party who reasonably and detrimentally relied on a promise to enforce that promise even though no valid contract was formed. But here, the contractor's reliance on the homeowner's contractual promise is irrelevant.

Educational objective:
An accord requires consideration to be valid. That consideration can only be worth less than what was agreed to in the original contract if (1) there is a good-faith dispute as to the amount owed or (2) the new consideration is of a different type than what was owed under the original contract.

解除合同义务的方式


完全履行合同义务
履行不能、履行不切实际或目的落空
免除（仅限书面形式）
双方合意解除
替代合同
不起诉合同或协议
和解与清偿
债务更新
助记词：FIRM SCAN
解除合同义务的一种方法是通过和解（新合同）与清偿（履行和解协议）。当合同双方同意给予并接受某种不同的东西以清偿其现有的合同义务时，便达成了和解。由于和解是一份新合同，它必须有对价支持。如果新的对价价值低于原合同中约定的价值，那么只有在以下情况下，该对价才足够：
  • 对所欠金额存在善意争议 或
  • 新的对价与原合同下所欠的类型不同（例如，以货物代替现金）。


在本案中，房主提议支付$35,000，以完全清偿其向承包商支付$50,000的合同义务。承包商同意了这一较低的金额（和解），房主也支付了该金额（清偿）。由于房主善意地相信承包商的工程存在瑕疵并且偏离了图纸（善意争议），房主支付的$35,000构成了足够的对价，从而形成有效的和解（选项D）。因此，承包商很可能不会胜诉。

(选项B) 工程的合理价值仅为$35,000这一事实，并不能免除房主支付$50,000合同价款的义务。相反，房主的义务通过和解（一份$35,000的新合同）与清偿（支付$35,000）而得以解除。

(选项C) “禁止反言”原则允许合理且不利地依赖某项承诺的一方强制执行该承诺，即使没有形成有效的合同。但在本案中，承包商对房主合同承诺的依赖是无关紧要的。

教学目标：
和解协议需要有对价才有效。只有在以下两种情况下，该对价的价值才可以低于原合同中的约定：(1) 对所欠金额存在善意争议，或 (2) 新的对价与原合同下所欠的类型不同。

References

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 281 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (accord and satisfaction).

Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 74 cmt. c (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that payment of a disputed amount is consideration for a return promise).

MBE Contracts 解析

Accord and Satisfaction (和解与清偿)
📚 核心考点：和解与清偿 本题考察的是合同法中关于债务解除的机制，特别是Accord and Satisfaction（和解与清偿）以及Consideration（对价）在解决争议债务中的应用。

⚖️ 法律规则解析

在普通法下，要通过支付较少金额来解除全部债务，必须满足以下条件：

🚫 一般原则 (Pre-existing Duty Rule)

如果债务是确定且无争议的 (Liquidated and Undisputed)，债务人承诺支付少于欠款的金额，不能构成免除剩余债务的有效对价。债权人收钱后仍可追讨余额。

✅ 本题例外：善意争议 (Good Faith Dispute)

如果双方对债务金额存在善意争议 (Good Faith Dispute)，或者债务金额未确定 (Unliquidated)：

双方达成协议支付一个折衷金额（Accord），并实际支付（Satisfaction），则原合同义务被解除。

关键点：争议必须是“善意”的，但不要求争议方在事实上是正确的。

🔍 案情应用

在本案中：

  1. 原合同：总价 $50,000。
  2. 争议：房主善意地相信 (Honestly believed) 工程有瑕疵。尽管事实上承包商完全履行了合同，但房主的主观信念是诚实的。
  3. 和解：房主提议支付 $35,000 以了结全部索赔，承包商接受并收到了款项。

因为存在善意争议，房主放弃“拒绝付款并在法庭上抗辩”的权利，这就是一种法律上的受损（Legal Detriment），构成了新协议的对价 (Consideration)。

✅ 正确答案：选项 A

承包商不会胜诉。因为房主对欠款金额提出了善意争议 (Good Faith Dispute)。这使得 $35,000 的支付成为了有效的和解对价，从而解除了剩余的债务。

❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？

选项 B (错误)： 虽然工程的合理价值是 $35,000，但这属于不当得利或准合同（Restitution/Quasi-contract）的概念。本案中有有效的合同和有效的和解协议，应直接执行协议约定，而非按市场价值计算。
选项 C (错误)： 此选项涉及“禁止反言” (Promissory Estoppel)。只有在没有有效合同（缺乏对价）时才考虑此原则。这里已经形成了有效的和解合同（有对价），因此不需要援引禁止反言。
选项 D (错误)： 这是最强的干扰项。它陈述了“既存义务原则”（支付已欠的钱不是对价）。但它忽略了本题的关键事实：争议的存在。如果房主没有善意争议，选项D就是对的。但在有争议的情况下，妥协本身就是对价。
💡 MBE 考试技巧
看到“支付较少金额以结清全款”的题目时，立即寻找关键词：
1. "Honestly believed" 或 "Good faith dispute" ➡️ 和解有效，余额不可追讨。
2. "Admitted he owed" 或无争议事实 ➡️ 和解无效（缺乏对价），余额可追讨。
不要纠结于房主的看法是否符合客观事实，只要他是诚实的，争议就是有效的。
MBE Contracts Review | QID: Q81829

questions.question:
A wallpaper hanger sent a general contractor this fax:
"Will do all paperhanging on the doctor's new building, per owner's specs, for $14,000 if you accept within reasonable time after main contract awarded."
Three competitors sent the general contractor similar bids to hang wallpaper in the doctor's building in the respective amounts of $18,000, $19,000, and $20,000. The general contractor used the wallpaper hanger's $14,000 figure in preparing and submitting her own sealed bid on the doctor's building. Before the bids were opened, the wallpaper hanger truthfully advised the general contractor that the former's sub-bid had been based on a $4,000 computational error and was therefore revoked. Shortly thereafter, the general contractor was awarded the doctor's building construction contract and subsequently contracted with a competitor to wallpaper the building for a price of $18,000.
The general contractor then sued the wallpaper hanger to recover $4,000.
Which of the following, if proved, would most strengthen the general contractor's prospect of recovery?

choices.a: After the wallpaper hanger's notice of revocation, the general contractor made a reasonable effort to subcontract with another paperhanger at the lowest possible price.
choices.b: The general contractor dealt with all of her subcontractors in good faith and without seeking to renegotiate (lower) the prices they had bid.
choices.c: The general contractor had been required by the owner to submit a bid bond in the amount of $50,000 and could not have withdrawn or amended her bid on the main contract without forfeiting that bond.
choices.d: The wallpaper hanger was negligent in erroneously calculating the amount of his sub-bid.
